interface.title: Ecosystem State Forecaster
interface.field: Remote sensing / vegetation ecology (satellite NDVI forecasting over Australian biomes)
interface.stage_of_work: Checking model results: out-of-sample skill of forecasting models against simple baselines
interface.what_it_is_for: Compare how well ML models (gbt, convlstm, gnn, ensemble) forecast next month's NDVI against persistence and seasonal climatology, across four Australian biomes and two satellite records, with monthly maps of actual, forecast and error.

data.note: Precomputed forecasts in the app's bundled NetCDF files: 4 biomes (Sunshine Coast subtropical, Daintree tropical rainforest, Alice Springs arid, Kosciuszko alpine) × 2 records (Sentinel-2 2015–2026, Landsat 1988–2026). There are 12 test months (2025-08 to 2026-07) on a coarsened pixel grid (for example 75×60 at Sunshine Coast). No upload or fetch is needed.

tree.general: Decide whether learned forecasting models beat simple baselines, and where and why
tree.specific: Decide whether GBT, ConvLSTM, GNN and the ensemble beat seasonal climatology for next-month NDVI in four Australian biomes, and how the answer depends on the length of the satellite record

features.specific: 'Do the models beat climatology?' chart: bars of skill vs climatology for gbt, convlstm, gnn and ensemble at Sunshine Coast, Daintree, Alice Springs and Kosciuszko. The Satellite record radio switches between Sentinel-2 and Landsat, and the caption below rewrites its conclusion to match (on Landsat the caption's 'models win in every biome' holds for GBT and the ensemble, not for convlstm or gnn).

screens_never_reached: 'One pixel through time' chart (pixel forecast trajectory vs actual NDVI, persistence and climatology): on every page load it shows ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'scipy'. The error comes from the server's xarray .interp(level=...) on conformal_q in series_fig (screens/004.webp, screens/005.webp).

Conformal prediction interval band and observed-coverage readout: these sit in, or after, the crashed time-series section. Script execution stops at the error, so nothing below 'One pixel through time' renders.
not_done: Inspect a single pixel's forecast trajectory over time against actual NDVI, persistence and climatology: blocked by the missing scipy module on the server. The pixel sliders only move the map marker (screens/019.webp).

Check whether the conformal interval is well calibrated: the Confidence level slider (50–99) moves and its tooltip says it redraws from stored conformal quantiles. At 90, 50 and 99 nothing visible changed because its output is behind the same scipy error (screens/021.webp, screens/023.webp, screens/048.webp).
Pick a pixel by clicking a map: the maps are static matplotlib images, and clicking one did nothing (screens/047.webp). Pixels can only be chosen with the sliders.

Quirk: after switching biome and then satellite record, the Forecast month slider showed 2026-07 while the panel rendered 2025-09. Moving the slider brought them back in line (screens/042.webp, screens/045.webp).
Changing the biome resets the Forecast month to the latest month and the pixel to the grid centre (screens/039.webp).

Models multiselect 'Clear all': the run's screens show an empty selection afterwards (screens/028.webp, screens/029.webp, screens/031.webp), but the replay found it only opened the dropdown; removing chips one by one does work. Which behaviour is real is unresolved.
